Progressive streaming (also called progressive download or HTTP progressive streaming) is a technique where media content is sent to the client in a way that allows playback to begin before the entire file has been downloaded. This is commonly used for video and audio content.

Why it improves perceived latency:

1. First, the client can start rendering/playing content as soon as enough data has arrived, rather than waiting for the entire file to download. This reduces the time-to-first-pixel or time-to-first-byte that matters for user experience.

2. Second, by overlapping download and playback, the perceived latency (the time from user action to visible/audible result) is reduced because the user sees content sooner.

Sentence 2: By overlapping download and playback, it reduces the perceived wait time (time-to-first-pixel), making the experience feel faster even if total transfer time is unchanged.
